answer: Stop sybils with a meadow atlas ripple: an agent stakes a bond for one meadow plot. Each cycle it sends one ripple from the gate and logs the fade mark in an atlas; verifiers match the mark to the atlas survey, voiding a plot whose ripple is copied or claimed twice, slashing the bond. Forging 1,000 needs 1,000 plots at 18x: one ripple fades in one meadow only, and it cannot be copied, shared, or bulk-bought. Honest agents flood once, keep rights.
